name: Soundgarden
label: Sub Pop
lede: A sculpture that moans in the wind gave them their name, and one night at the Rainbow Tavern gave Sub Pop its first backer. They were the first Seattle band signed to a major label, split in 1997 after a bass went flying in Honolulu, and are still finishing the last songs Chris Cornell sang on.

eras.title: A drummer who sang, and a sculpture that hums
eras.text: Kim Thayil and Hiro Yamamoto, two friends from Park Forest, Illinois, found a Seattle drummer who could really sing. Two years on, Soundgarden had a proper drummer, a manager and three songs on the compilation that first put a name to the Seattle sound.

years.h: Chris Cornell, Kim Thayil and Hiro Yamamoto start Soundgarden
years.p: Cornell sings from behind the drum kit, Yamamoto plays bass and Thayil guitar. Cornell and Yamamoto had already played together in a covers band called the Shemps.

years.h: The name comes from a sculpture that hums
years.p: A Sound Garden is a 1983 sculpture of pipes on the NOAA grounds beside Magnuson Park, and it makes eerie tones when the wind blows through them.

years.h: Scott Sundquist takes the drums and Cornell steps out front
years.p: With [[Scott Sundquist|2a1cc59e-5465-417c-af9e-115a432e614b]] behind the kit, Cornell can finally sing standing up.

years.cap: Cornell, Thayil and Yamamoto on stage, Seattle, 1985
q: That was one of the best shows I've seen in my whole life.
years.h: The Rainbow Tavern night that turns a booker into a label owner
years.p: Jonathan Poneman, booking the Rainbow Tavern near the University of Washington, watches a bare-chested Cornell and decides to put money behind the band.
years.xp:
Poneman was a KCMU radio DJ booking weekly showcases at the Rainbow to raise money for the station. He added Soundgarden to the bill a little reluctantly, on another band's singer's recommendation. They had been together about seven months and had nothing released. Skin Yard, Matt Cameron's band, played the same night.

Afterward he walked up to Cornell and introduced himself. Years later he summed up what the night did to him: "I was a struggling someday-to-be record-label head."

He teamed with [[Bruce Pavitt|f5230572-06e4-453c-a1dd-7a4b560da3bb]], who had known Thayil back in the Midwest and was running Sub Pop as a fanzine and cassette series without money to press records. Poneman put in $20,000, and Sub Pop became a label.

years.h: Skin Yard's Matt Cameron takes the drums and Susan Silver starts managing
years.p: [[Matt Cameron|07e93890-46a1-4ebd-9a70-3988a2135d87]], drummer for [[Skin Yard|0119843b-4d56-47b6-ac0d-11528259bf0a]], replaces Sundquist, who leaves to spend time with his family. [[Susan Silver|bdd26cdc-cbc9-4def-8d74-d15e871e5129]] becomes the band's manager.

years.h: Deep Six puts three songs next to the Melvins and Green River
years.p: C/Z Records' compilation also holds [[Malfunkshun|71f4a8ff-97ba-47c6-a729-7f87de77c796]], Skin Yard and the U-Men, and is among the first records to put a name on the Seattle sound.

eras.title: The label they inspired puts out their first records
eras.text: Soundgarden's first records came out on the label they had inspired, with Jack Endino behind the board. Then Greg Ginn's SST put out an album, and A&M signed the band before it was even out.

years.cap: Soundgarden among the lily pads, Seattle, 1987
years.h: Hunted Down is one of the first records on Sub Pop
years.p: Backed with Nothing to Say, it is Soundgarden's first single, out two years after Poneman first saw them at the Rainbow.

years.h: Jack Endino records Screaming Life at Reciprocal
years.p: The six-song EP comes out of the Seattle studio that would soon make Bleach for [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]].
years.xp: SPIN reports the EP came out on limited-edition orange vinyl.

years.h: An Ohio Players cover leads the Fopp EP
years.p: Soundgarden's second Sub Pop EP opens with its version of the Ohio Players' Fopp, recorded with Steve Fisk.

years.h: A&M Records signs Soundgarden before their SST album is out
years.p: Per Wikipedia, they are the first band of the Seattle scene on a major label, and the signing lands months ahead of Ultramega OK.

years.h: Ultramega OK lands on SST and a Grammy ballot
years.p: The debut album is nominated for the first Best Metal Performance Grammy, in 1990, which goes to [[Metallica|65f4f0c5-ef9e-490c-aee3-909e7ae6b2ab]]. Its label is [[Greg Ginn|4f35de64-27ab-4426-95fd-8d454cda4e48]]'s SST.

eras.title: Two bassists out, one found, and a record for a dead friend
eras.text: On A&M the band got louder, lost two bassists in a year and found Ben Shepherd. Then came the wrong tour with Guns N' Roses, a tribute album for Andrew Wood, and Badmotorfinger.

years.h: Louder Than Love is the first grunge album on the Billboard 200
years.p: The A&M debut peaks at No. 108, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Yamamoto goes back to college and Jason Everman takes his bass
years.p: Frustrated that he isn't contributing much, Yamamoto quits. Everman, months out of [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]], takes over.

years.h: Mother Love Bone's Andrew Wood dies at 24
years.p: [[Andrew Wood|400e187f-31b0-473d-a4c3-685d38229274]], Cornell's former roommate, dies of a heroin overdose. Cornell writes songs for him that become Temple of the Dog.

years.h: Everman is fired, and Ben Shepherd gets the bass
years.p: Everman is let go after the Louder Than Love tour. Shepherd, who had once nearly played guitar in Nirvana, takes the job.
years.xp: Everman later called the firing heartbreaking, and eventually joined the U.S. Army. Shepherd had befriended Kurt Cobain at an Olympia party; he said he was meant to play lead guitar for Nirvana, but they stayed a trio.

years.h: Cornell's tribute to Andrew Wood becomes Temple of the Dog
years.p: Stone Gossard, Jeff Ament and Mike McCready, of the band that became [[Pearl Jam|83b9cbe7-9857-49e2-ab8e-b57b01038103]], play on it. A new singer, [[Eddie Vedder|1a60d6dd-9d3e-40fc-a66d-3184f9ee0d61]], duets with Cornell on Hunger Strike.

years.h: Badmotorfinger reaches No. 39 and goes double platinum
years.p: Odd time signatures, their heaviest riffs yet. MTV bans the Jesus Christ Pose video, and the band gets death threats on tour in the U.K., per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Soundgarden live on the Badmotorfinger tour
years.h: Guns N' Roses' crew nickname their opening act Frowngarden
years.p: Soundgarden open arenas on the Use Your Illusion tour and stay out of the excess. The crew's joke is that they never joined the party.
years.xp:
Silver says that when she announced the offer, "They didn't say a word. After about 30 seconds... one of them said, 'What's in the box?'"

Shepherd was blunt: "I'm a punk rocker, man." Cameron said Axl Rose made the band wait an hour or two to go on. His verdict on the whole run: "An eye-opening lesson as far as how not to tour if you become successful."

years.cap: Cornell singing on the Badmotorfinger tour, c. 1992
years.h: Birth Ritual plays in Cameron Crowe's Singles
years.p: Soundgarden appear in the Seattle film, and play the main stage at Lollapalooza that summer. The song is on the soundtrack next to Cornell's solo track Seasons.

eras.title: A number one record and a bass in the air
eras.text: Superunknown made Soundgarden one of the biggest rock bands in the world. Two years later the band was arguing over how heavy to be, and a bass thrown in Honolulu marked the last show of the tour before the split.

years.h: Superunknown debuts at No. 1
years.p: The fourth album goes six times platinum, by far their biggest, on singles including Spoonman, The Day I Tried to Live, Black Hole Sun, My Wave and Fell on Black Days.
years.xp: Spoonman features [[Artis the Spoonman|c75a51e1-2c04-4663-a664-bafe0aebf23d]], a Seattle street performer, playing spoons. The Black Hole Sun video won Best Metal/Hard Rock Video at the 1994 MTV Video Music Awards and the Clio for alternative music video the next year.

years.h: Soundgarden go home from the 1995 Grammys with two
years.p: Spoonman wins Best Metal Performance and Black Hole Sun wins Best Hard Rock Performance.

years.h: Down on the Upside brings acoustic instruments and arguments
years.p: The band wanted to try other sounds and argued over how far to move from heavy riffs. It debuts at No. 2, and they headline Lollapalooza with [[Metallica|65f4f0c5-ef9e-490c-aee3-909e7ae6b2ab]].

years.h: Ben Shepherd throws his bass in the air and walks off in Honolulu
years.p: His gear fails at the last show of the tour, and he leaves the stage. Cornell comes back alone to finish.

years.h: Soundgarden announce they are done after thirteen years
years.p: Thayil says the dissatisfaction had been obvious for about half a year. The hits collection A-Sides follows that November.
years.xp: Cameron joined [[Pearl Jam|83b9cbe7-9857-49e2-ab8e-b57b01038103]] in 1998. Cornell made solo records and fronted [[Audioslave|020bfbb4-05c3-4c86-b372-17825c262094]] with members of [[Rage Against the Machine|3798b104-01cb-484c-a3b0-56adc6399b80]] from 2001 to 2007.

eras.title: School is back in session
eras.text: Soundgarden came back on a tweet in 2010, toured the world again and made one more album, King Animal. Then Cornell died in Detroit in May 2017.

years.big: The 12-year break is over and school is back in session.
years.h: Soundgarden's comeback arrives as a tweet
years.p: Cornell posts it on Twitter on New Year's Day, 13 years after the band split.

years.h: Billed as Nudedragons, they play their first show in 13 years
years.p: The Showbox at the Market in Seattle gets the anagram billing. Soundgarden headline Lollapalooza in Chicago that August.

years.h: King Animal ends a 16-year wait for new music
years.p: The sixth album, with singles Been Away Too Long, By Crooked Steps and Halfway There, is the last released in Cornell's lifetime.

years.h: Chris Cornell dies in Detroit, hours after a Fox Theatre show
years.p: He was 52. He was found in his room at the MGM Grand Detroit, and the Wayne County medical examiner ruled it suicide by hanging.

eras.title: The last songs, fought over and finished
eras.text: Without Chris Cornell the band said it was done, then spent years in court with his widow over seven songs he'd sung on. The settlement brought the survivors back together, a Hall of Fame night with their original bassist, and a final album in progress.

years.big: There were four of us and now there's three of us.
years.h: Kim Thayil says Soundgarden is unlikely to go on
years.p: Thayil tells the Seattle Times in October that touring or recording as Soundgarden looks unlikely, with catalog work about all that's left.

years.h: A tribute to Chris Cornell fills the Forum in Inglewood
years.p: At I Am the Highway, Thayil, Cameron and Shepherd play eight songs with guest singers including [[Taylor Momsen|d1ecf86c-3d89-420e-b8c1-bceb6b101c61]] and [[Brandi Carlile|baf05baf-69fb-47dd-93c2-033536b8c385]].

years.big: A new partnership between the two parties.
years.h: Soundgarden and Vicky Cornell settle their lawsuits
years.p: Their joint statement of April 17 calls it an amicable out of court resolution. It clears the way for the band to finish the unreleased songs.
years.xp:
Vicky Cornell sued the surviving members and their business manager in 2019, saying they tried to "strong-arm" her over seven unreleased recordings by withholding estate royalties. The band countersued two months later, saying she had no authority to keep the tracks off their final album.

More filings followed: a May 2020 counterclaim over the January 2019 tribute concert, dropped that July; her second suit in February 2021 over the value of her stake in the band; a fight over social media accounts that March.

years.h: Nudedragons return for a Seattle Children's Hospital benefit
years.p: The surviving members, with vocalist Shaina Shepherd, play their first show since the 2019 tribute, under the anagram they used in 2010.

years.cap: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, 2025
years.h: Soundgarden enter the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Yamamoto back on bass
years.p: Yamamoto plays with the band for the first time in 36 years. Rusty Cage has Momsen and Mike McCready; Black Hole Sun has Carlile and [[Jerry Cantrell|960eb93f-e73c-4df8-864d-08a06c2dcc11]].
years.xp: Jim Carrey presented the induction. Thayil, Cameron and Shepherd played two songs with the guests.

years.h: Cameron says the final album is over halfway done
years.p: Eight songs were recorded with Cornell, and the survivors are working with producer Terry Date. The target is 2027, ten years after his death.
years.xp: In June 2026 Cameron told interviewers they were "definitely over halfway done with" the remaining songs.
